newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan airline opens China office, eyes air links.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan airline opens China office, eyes air links.

text.p: Taiwan's EVA Airways said on Friday it had opened an office in Beijing, positioning itself to take a slice of China's growing aviation market despite Taipei's ban on direct air links to the mainland.
"Our Chinese head office was opened in Beijing on March 12 and we are prepared to tap the vast mainland aviation market," EVA Airways assistant manager Chiu Ke-tai told Reuters.

EVA, a unit of shipping giant Evergreen Marine, took the step as Taiwan and China appeared to be taking serious steps toward establishing the first direct shipping links since 1949 when they were split by a civil war.
Taiwan executives who have invested some US$30 billion in mainland industry have been pressing Taipei and Beijing to allow direct air and shipping links to help them save costs.

Chiu said EVA, Taiwan's second-biggest airline after China Airlines, hoped to cooperate with mainland aviation firms to develop passenger and cargo business, maintenance and personnel training with flight schools in China.

Taiwan has banned direct links with China since 1949. But in the face of huge business demand, Taiwan has agreed to allow limited direct shipping links with China. China is reportedly close to approving a batch of applications by Taipei shipping firms seeking to make the first direct crossing of the Taiwan strait.
